What's new in Callout 0.8.5

Version 0.8.5 Alpha

0.8.5 fixes something that has been in every Callout since the first text was typed and only showed once the type got big: the white halo around text had sharp, mitred corners, and at every pointed vertex — the top of an M, the apex of an A, the points of a W — the mitre ran on into a spike. At 24 pixels the spike is a pixel and nobody sees it. On a large picture, with the captions scaled up to match, the spikes become horns. The halo now has round corners. Nothing moves; every Card, old and new, simply loses the horns.

The same report asked about spacing. Half the halo sits outside each letter, so each gap between two letters loses a halo’s width, and on heavy capitals that is most of the gap. Text made from 0.8.5 on gets that width back, so the gaps read as the typeface designed them. Text on existing Cards keeps its layout exactly — a Card you made yesterday does not re-flow — and the Stroke slider still governs both the halo and the room it takes.

Fixed

  • No more horns on the halo. The outline around text is stroked with round corners, so pointed letters no longer grow spikes at large sizes. Every Card, with nothing else changed.
  • New text gets the room its halo takes. Letter spacing on text made from now on widens by the halo’s width, following the Stroke slider; turn the halo off and the spacing returns to the face’s own. Older text keeps its layout.

Also fixed

Small things found while building the two fixes above, folded in because the release was open anyway.

  • Overlapping spotlights dim once. Where two spotlight regions overlapped, the overlap was dimmed twice; it is now as bright as the rest of the lit area, and Lift applies once too.
  • New callouts on an older Card come out Beside. A Card saved without any callouts reopened with the old Legend style waiting for it, so callouts drawn on it later collected in a legend instead of sitting beside their markers. Cards that already carry Legend callouts keep them.
  • Dragging a group moves a magnifier’s source too. A detached magnifier dragged as part of a group left the spot it magnifies behind; it now travels with the lens, as it does when dragged alone.
  • Standard arrows select by their own shape. The hit test for a standard-headed arrow was using the tapered arrow’s shape.
  • The text cursor stays on the letters when you are zoomed out. The editor now lays out text at the same size as the canvas and scales the view, so the caret cannot drift from the letters at small zoom levels, and the selection highlight covers exactly the letters it selects; its frame no longer narrows for an instant between keystrokes. One side effect: the caret itself is drawn thinner when you are zoomed well out.
  • Colours are exact from the first stroke. A freshly drawn annotation and the same annotation reopened from disk differed by a hair in colour; they are identical now. Existing Cards are unchanged.
  • Clear All Annotations keeps pictures, on purpose. A picture you added to a Card is content, not markup, so the command leaves it where it is. Unchanged, now written down.

What's new in Callout 0.8.4

Version 0.8.4 Alpha

0.8.4 fixes one thing that two bug reports described from different sides: copying markup. Until now ⌘C always copied the finished image and ⌘V always made a new Card from whatever image was on the clipboard — there was no way to copy an arrow or a text at all. Select a text, press ⌘C then ⌘V, and you got a second Card that looked exactly like the first, with every arrow and text baked into its pixels, and nothing said so. From then on the “arrows” could not be selected, because they were no longer arrows, and clicking a baked-in text with the Text tool made a new one on top of it.

Now ⌘C with something selected copies that markup, ⌘V puts the copy back on the Card beside the original — or onto any other Card — and ⌘X cuts. ⌘C still carries the finished image for Slack, Mail and everything else, so the capture–mark–copy–paste loop is exactly what it was. With nothing selected, ⌘C copies the finished image as before, and pasting a plain image still makes a new Card — it just says so now.

Copy and paste

  • Copy and paste markup. Select an arrow, a text, a shape — or several — and ⌘C copies them; ⌘V pastes the copy nudged beside the original, or at the same place on another Card; paste again and it steps along. ⌘X cuts. Undo takes back a paste or a cut in one step.
  • The finished image still rides along. ⌘C with a selection puts both on the clipboard: Callout reads its own markup, every other app receives the image, so pasting into Slack works whether or not something was selected.
  • Pasting an image says what it did. An image on the clipboard still becomes a new Card; the status bar now says “Pasted as a new Card”, so a duplicate can never again look like nothing happened.
  • Cut, Copy and Paste in the Edit menu know when they apply. Cut needs a selection; Paste needs something pasteable.
  • Also asked for, and not in this release: a way to select without a tool, or Tab through the objects on a Card. Logged for discussion.

What's new in Callout 0.8.3

Version 0.8.3 Alpha

0.8.3 fixes one thing a bug report named: a large picture — a phone photo, a scan, anything far bigger than a screenshot — made Callout stall for seconds after every edit. The cause was the autosave: it rendered and encoded the whole picture on the main thread, each time, with a wasteful detour on the way. Saving now happens in the background, encodes directly, and a burst of edits produces one write; drawing keeps a screen-sized copy of the picture so dragging stays smooth. Screenshots were never affected, which is why nobody saw it until a photo arrived. Measuring it turned up a second thing hiding underneath: a Card with any markup on it had been saving itself after every click, not only after every change, because each save thought the Card was new. It no longer does; a click that changes nothing writes nothing.

Also: the bug reporter’s event history no longer fills up with hourly update checks, so the sixty lines it keeps are the ones that matter. Nothing else changed.

Fixed

  • Large pictures no longer stall the app. Saving runs in the background and encodes directly; a run of edits yields one write; drawing uses a screen-sized copy of the picture. Everything is still saved exactly as before.
  • A click that changes nothing writes nothing. A Card with markup used to re-save on every click; it saves only when something changed, which also means Dropbox stops re-syncing a picture that did not change.
  • Bug reports keep the events that matter. An hourly update check that finds nothing is one line in the history, not two.
